archetype.name: Play-In Exit (stars-when-healthy)
archetype.definition: A team that was a winning side through January with its stars on the floor, then slid to a losing record and went out in the play-in, the first losing season in its recent history.

report.headline: 27-23 after January, then a collapse that left only a play-in exit

recap.finish: 37-45, fourth in the Pacific; lost in the play-in
recap.body:
This was a team whose best version showed up in pieces. With Stephen Curry and Jimmy Butler on the floor, Golden State looked like the club that won 48 games a year ago. Curry posted a 63.7 TS % with a 5.4 BPM and made the All-Star team. Butler's +11.6 On-Off was the loudest number on the roster. But Curry played 43 games, Butler 38 and Kristaps Porziņģis 32. The season-long profile came out almost exactly average: an ORtg of 115 (18th) against a DRtg of 115.6 (17th), for a -0.6 Net Rtg that ranked 20th.

The first half held up. A 4-2 October, a .500-ish November and winning months in December and January had them 27-23 at the end of January. Then it came apart. February went 4-6, March 5-10 and April 1-6. They finished with a 3-7 last ten and a 1-4 last five, scoring 3.21 fewer points a game than their season norm over that final stretch. Three of those last-ten losses came by six points or fewer, including a 116-117 loss to Houston. Two of the late losses, including one of the two meetings, came against a Sacramento side that went 22-60.

The identity was a shooting team. Its 3PA Rate of 49.7 led the league and sat 8.2 points above average. The efficiency held, with an eFG % that ranked 13th and a TS % that ranked 11th, despite only a league-average 3P %. What dragged it was the rest of the possession game. A TOV % of 13.8 ranked 27th, and a FT Rate of 23.8 ranked 24th, so the offense gave the ball away and rarely got cheap points. The defense forced turnovers well (Opp TOV % 14, 5th) but slipped from 7th to 17th in Def Rank. DRtg went from 111.7 to 115.6. A DRB % that ranked 22nd kept handing opponents second chances, and opposing guards found room: both PG and SG scoring against them ranked 24th.

The grades tell the same story. Wings graded A+, but that group is essentially Butler's 38 games. Malevy Leons, the only other listed wing, posted a -11.5 On-Off in his minutes. The backcourt (B-) leaned on Brandin Podziemski playing all 82 games, plus Moses Moody's +4.7 On-Off. The frontcourt graded C. Draymond Green logged its most minutes with a 54.0 TS %, a -1.4 BPM and a -4 On-Off. Gui Santos (60.9 TS %) and Quinten Post (+3.4 On-Off) were the more productive bigs.

Luck didn't help either. The point differential of -46 implies 40 wins, and the W vs Pt Diff of -3 ranked 24th. That isn't the difference between a play-in and a top-six seed, but it does mean this was closer to a .500 team than 37-45 suggests. It still marks a sharp step down from four straight winning seasons in the history shown.

highlights.title: Curry and Butler still elite
highlights.body: When available, the two stars played at a top level. Curry posted a 63.7 TS % on a 32.5 USG %, and Butler's 64.6 TS % came with an +11.6 On-Off and a team-high 5.7 Win Shares in just 38 games. The problem was never their quality, only how rarely they shared a full season's worth of floor time.

highlights.title: League's most three-heavy offense
highlights.body: Nobody took a bigger share of their shots from deep: the 3PA Rate of 49.7 ranked 1st, 8.2 above the league. That volume kept the shot quality decent even with an average 3P %, producing an eFG % that ranked 13th. The approach is sustainable as long as Curry and the shooters are on the floor.

highlights.title: Podziemski's every-night reliability
highlights.body: On a roster that kept losing its headliners, Brandin Podziemski played all 82 games and led the team in minutes. He produced 5.1 Win Shares at a 58.3 TS %. He was more steady than dominant, but he was the one constant in a season defined by absences.

lowlights.title: Post-January collapse
lowlights.body: At 27-23 through January this was a playoff-track team. It then posted losing records in February, March and April, closing 1-6 in the final month. Over the last ten games the per-game differential ran 5.34 points worse than the season mark. The slide lined up with a roster whose top players appeared in roughly half the schedule or less.

lowlights.title: Defense and glass slipped
lowlights.body: DRtg rose from 111.7 last season to 115.6, and Def Rank fell from 7th to 17th. A DRB % of 72.9 (22nd) meant too many second chances. Forcing turnovers (5th in Opp TOV %) masked some of it, but this was a middling defense that leaked on the boards.

lowlights.title: Turnovers, no free throws, thin frontcourt
lowlights.body: A TOV % of 13.8 ranked 27th and a FT Rate of 23.8 ranked 24th, so possessions were wasted and easy points scarce. The C-graded frontcourt contributed to it: its biggest-minutes player, Draymond Green, carried a -4 On-Off and a 54.0 TS %.

arc.note: Steady winning months carried them to 27-23 by the end of January. After that, each month was a losing one, ending with a 1-6 April and a play-in loss.

recap.nextYear: The numbers say this core still wins when its stars play. Curry and Butler were the two best impact players on the roster by BPM and On-Off, and the A+ wing grade is Butler's alone, with no real depth behind him. The frontcourt (C) is the clearest area of need, both for rebounding and for production beyond Santos and Post. Ball security and getting to the line were bottom-tier, which is fixable regardless of health. A W vs Pt Diff of -3, with a margin worth 40 wins, says some of the record was bad luck in close games. But a 37-45 team with a negative Net Rtg and a defense that fell from 7th to 17th can't count on luck alone to get back to the 48-win level.

confidence.note: Full 82-game season; availability of stars clouds what the healthy roster is.
